questions.solution_en:
These modal verbs (should/might/could/would/had to) in indirect speech are changed to (shall/may/can/will/must) in direct speech.

Example: She said that she could speak ten languages. (Indirect Speech)

She said, "I can speak ten languages". (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'That' will be removed from the sentence and inverted commas will be introduced.

'He' will be changed to 'I'.

'Would' will be changed to 'will'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Harry said, "I will not be in town on Friday".

options_en: James asked, "Did you complete the assignment?"
James asked, "Have you completed the assignment?"
James asked, "Will you complete the assignment?"

questions.solution_en:
In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we remove the inverted commas and add the conjunction "If" or "Whether" in the Indirect Speech and the verb/s "Is/are/am/was/were" before the subject, in Direct Speech.

For example:

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Perfect tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present Perfect tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Asked if - Asked

Had - have

I - You

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He always says to me, "I am perturbed."
options_en: He always tells me that he is mostly perturbed.
He always tells me that he is perturbed by change.
He always tells me that he is perturbed.
He always tells me that he is going to be perturbed.
questions.solution_en:
To convert the direct speech sentence "He always says to me, 'I am perturbed'" to indirect speech:

The reporting verb "says" is present tense, so the tense of the reported clause ("I am perturbed") remains present ("is").

The phrase "to me" indicates the verb should be "tells" (as "say to someone" becomes "tell someone" in indirect speech).

The pronoun "I" changes to "he" to match the subject.

The conjunction "that" is added, and quotation marks are removed.

The direct speech "I am perturbed" becomes "he is perturbed," making the sentence: "He always tells me that he is perturbed."

Checking the options:

Option 1: "He always tells me that he is mostly perturbed" adds "mostly," which is not in the original.

Option 2: "He always tells me that he is perturbed by change" adds "by change," which is not implied.

Option 3: "He always tells me that he is perturbed" accurately reflects the original sentence.

Option 4: "He always tells me that he is going to be perturbed" shifts to future tense, which is incorrect.

Thus, option 3 is the correct choice.

questions.q_en: Select the option with the correct use of past tense.
options_en: The renowned scientist were accepting the prestigious award at the ceremony held last month.
The renowned scientist accepted the prestigious award at the ceremony held last month.
The renowned scientist had been accepting the prestigious award at the ceremony held last month.
The renowned scientist have accepted the prestigious award at the ceremony held last month.
questions.solution_en:
The correct option is b).

This sentence correctly uses the simple past tense ("accepted"). This tense is used for actions that were completed at a specific, finished time in the past. The phrase "last month" clearly indicates a finished past time.

· Option (a): This has a subject-verb agreement error. The singular subject "scientist" requires the singular verb "was," not the plural "were."

· Option (c): This uses the past perfect continuous tense, which is for actions that were ongoing before another past action. It is not suitable for a single, completed event like this.

· Option (d): This incorrectly uses the present perfect tense ("have accepted"). This tense is for actions with a present connection, not for actions at a specified finished time like "last month." Also, the plural "have" is incorrect for the singular subject "scientist".

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

As a result of increasing population and expansion of residential areas, forest lands are being encroached. This is not all; even the wildlife is under extreme threat. As our fauna is facing a dearth of adequate shelter in forests, they are heading towards towns and hence get killed by hunters. Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction. The Black Buck is almost endangered and found only in two countries, Nepal and India. In India, this antelope is found in many national parks like Guindy National Park, Point Calimere and Vellandu sanctuaries of Tamil Nadu, Rollapadu of Andra Pradesh, few parts of Rajasthan and Haryana. As far as their habitat is concerned, they live in open grasslands, dry areas or thinly populated areas and near water resources. They live in the desert areas of Rajasthan and coastal areas because they cannot sustain cold climate. They are the fastest running animals on this planet. Further, this animal is active during the day but slows down in its activities after midday. They are social beings. Hence, they move with their herds, which can vary from 3 to 23 mates. They cohabit twice in a year and give birth twice in a year. Prior to independence, this antelope was extensively hunted which affected their population so much that this species has reached the stage of extinction in many parts of the country. Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. Hence, under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972, numerous stern measures have been taken. To specify a few, Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Bihar), Gir Forest National Park, Velavadar Wildlife Sanctuary (Gujarat), National Chambal Sanctuary, etc. Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife. There are some solutions to this problem but the best one is to boycott the products made from endangered species at an international level. This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That's a question.

What is the theme of this passage?
questions.solution_en:
The central theme of the passage is the threat to wildlife, particularly the Black Buck, which is "almost endangered" and at risk of extinction. The passage discusses the impact of habitat loss, historical and ongoing hunting, and conservation efforts, stating, "Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction," and focuses extensively on the Black Buck's status, habitat, and protection measures. While land encroachment and population growth are mentioned, they serve as causes contributing to the main issue of endangered species.

(b) Over-population: Population growth is noted briefly ("increasing population"), but it's a secondary factor leading to the main theme of wildlife endangerment, not the central focus.

(c) Forests and their uses: The passage does not discuss how forests are used but rather how their loss affects wildlife, making this option irrelevant.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said to me, "You would not live in peace if you did this to me."
options_en: He told me that I would not live in peace if I did that to him.
He told me that I would not live in peace if I had done that to him.
He told me that I would not live in peace if you had done that to me.
He told me that I could not live in peace if you had done that to me.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

For example:

He said, "Arya sent me a book." (Direct Speech)

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

When converting direct speech into indirect speech, the present modal verbs (should/might/could/would/ought to/had to) are not changed, and they remain the same in indirect speech.

Example: He said, "I should apologize to Jack for my bad behaviour." (Direct Speech)

He said that he should apologize to Jack for his bad behaviour". (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The pronoun 'you' and 'me' is changed into 'I' and 'him' respectively.

· The verb 'did' (past simple) is changed into 'had done' (past perfect).

· 'This' is changed into 'that' and 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): He told me that I would not live in peace if I had done that to him.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).
